{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "The goal is one paying customer in 90 days. B has sourced evidence that budget already exists in its category: Files.com bundles the same 'Expectations' feature in plans starting at $199/mo, and Nodinite charges about $3,600/yr. A's only sourced paid anchor is ReviewGuard at $1.99/mo, which covers Google Maps and TripAdvisor, not Reddit.",
    "A's brief names four free, actively maintained competitors, several of them open source. For the Reddit use case specifically, every named competitor is free. That leaves no sourced evidence that anyone pays to filter Reddit bots, and willingness to pay is exactly what the 90-day goal depends on.",
    "At B's hypothesized $49–199/mo, a single customer validates the business. A needs freemium conversion at $1.99–5/mo, and the brief says no competitor publishes conversion or revenue data, so getting even one payer is less predictable.",
    "B has a sourced gap in the market. The cheap competitor, WatchFor, checks server availability, not file arrival or content. Files.com and Definite bundle file-arrival monitoring inside larger platforms, which leaves room for a point solution aimed at teams on bare SFTP.",
    "A carries risks the brief itself flags that could make the product harmful or fragile: false positives that misflag real users as bots, and dependence on third-party page structures and Reddit's terms of service. B's main risk is commercial, either customers self-building or incumbents bundling. That risk can be tested quickly through direct outreach."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "The price hypothesis rests on ReviewGuard's $1.99/mo Pro tier. That product covers Amazon, Google Maps and TripAdvisor reviews, not Reddit. Every Reddit-specific competitor in the brief is free. A's demand quotes ('sick and tired of bots', 'taking time away from reddit') show frustration, not willingness to pay. So there is no sourced evidence that the core Reddit use case can earn money.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate. B has real weaknesses too. Its demand quotes are old (2012 and 2016). Its SEO cost claim is unsourced. Its own brief concedes the feature can be built with a cron job and Slack in an afternoon, and that incumbents are bundling it. The choice of B rests mainly on stronger evidence of willingness to pay and a lower bar for landing one customer, not on strong evidence of demand for B as a standalone product."
}
